facts.F1: Bug 6686 — Jira OAuth: write-back cannot write with read-only scopes. The Jira OAuth connection asks only for read scopes (read:jira-work, read:jira-user, board/sprint/issue/project read scopes, offline_access) in JiraOAuthProvider.cs. Write-back (Data Sync Mappings) on a Jira OAuth connection therefore cannot write: Jira refuses the update for lack of write:jira-work. Jira API-token connections are not affected. To check: confirm the failure on a Jira OAuth connection with a write-back mapping; then decide whether Jira OAuth should ask for write:jira-work only when write-back is set up, the same way as the Azure DevOps change in Story 6672. Found while preparing Story 6672. Maintainer decisions 2026-11-24: mirror the Azure DevOps change (ask write:jira-work only when write-back mappings are saved, record what Atlassian granted, show the Rights line and the Sign in again warning for Jira too); a Jira OAuth sign-in stored before rights were recorded counts as read-only; the write-consent warning names the connection's tracker (Jira or Azure DevOps).
facts.F10: The write-consent warning names the connection's own tracker (Jira or Azure DevOps) and keeps its Sign in again action
facts.F11: The write-consent warning names the connection's tracker, so a Jira OAuth connection is told it can only read from Jira
facts.F12: The connection settings page shows a Jira OAuth connection and an Azure DevOps OAuth connection whose sign-in may only read while write-back is set up
facts.F13: The Jira connection's warning reads: Write-back needs more rights. Lighthouse can only read from Jira with this sign-in. Sign in again to allow Lighthouse to write the mapped fields. The Azure DevOps connection's warning names Azure DevOps. Both keep the Sign in again button.
facts.F14: A Jira connection's warning names Azure DevOps, or names no tracker, or the Sign in again button is gone
facts.F15: Connecting a Jira OAuth connection asks Atlassian for write:jira-work only when write-back mappings are saved on that connection; a connection with no write-back mappings asks for the read scopes only.
facts.F16: Write-back on a Jira OAuth connection that was signed in without write rights sends nothing to Jira, including a connection signed in before rights were recorded.
facts.F17: That refused write-back attempt on a Jira OAuth connection without write rights writes exactly one warning to the log.
facts.F18: A Jira OAuth connection without write rights shows the rights as Rights Read, together with a Sign in again warning.
facts.F19: After the admin signs in again and Atlassian grants write:jira-work, write-back on that Jira OAuth connection sends the change to Jira.
facts.F2: Write-back works on a Jira OAuth connection: Lighthouse asks Atlassian for write rights only when write-back is set up, and shows when a Jira sign-in may only read.
facts.F20: Write-back on Azure DevOps OAuth connections and API-token connections keeps working as it did before this change.
facts.F21: The write-consent warning names the connection's own tracker, Jira or Azure DevOps, and never the other one.
facts.F22: The write-consent warning offers a Sign in again action on the connection it describes.
facts.F3: A Jira OAuth connection asks Atlassian for write:jira-work only when write-back mappings are saved on it; otherwise it asks for the read scopes only
facts.F4: Lighthouse records what Atlassian granted; write-back on a Jira OAuth sign-in without write rights, including a sign-in made before rights were recorded, sends nothing to Jira and logs one warning, and the connection shows Rights Read with the Sign in again warning
facts.F5: After the admin signs in again and Atlassian grants write:jira-work, write-back on the Jira OAuth connection sends the change; Azure DevOps OAuth and API-token connections keep their current behaviour
facts.F6: A Jira OAuth connection with write-back asks Atlassian for write:jira-work, records what Atlassian granted, and write-back on a Jira sign-in that may only read is not sent and is shown as needing a new sign-in
facts.F7: An admin signs in a Jira OAuth connection with and without write-back mappings, Atlassian answers the token request with a granted scope, and a write-back runs on that connection
facts.F8: Without write-back the sign-in asks Atlassian for the read scopes and offline_access only; with write-back it also asks for write:jira-work. A grant naming write:jira-work lets write-back send the change to Jira; a grant without it, or a Jira sign-in stored before rights were recorded, sends nothing, logs one warning, and the connection list says Rights Read and needsWriteConsent true. Azure DevOps OAuth and API-token connections behave as before.
facts.F9: The sign-in URL for a Jira connection with write-back lacks write:jira-work, or a read-only Jira grant (or an old Jira sign-in with no recorded rights) still sends a write-back to Jira, or the connection list shows no rights for a Jira OAuth connection
